comparisons.peer_summary: Risk ratings incorporate the obligor's industry, and the Firm manages credit risk by focusing on the diversification of industry and client exposures, paying particular attention to sectors with actual or potential credit concerns.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures focus on the management and diversification of industry exposures within the corporate loan portfolio. Goldman Sachs explicitly breaks down its corporate loan concentration percentages by industry (e.g., Technology, Media & Telecommunications at 24%), whereas JPMorgan describes its framework for managing these exposures by rating loans based on the obligor's industry and focusing on diversification to mitigate credit concerns.

sentences.text: • The top five industry concentrations for corporate loans as of December 2024 were 24% for technology, media & telecommunications, 16% for diversified industrials, 14% for real estate, 9% for financial institutions and 9% for healthcare.

As part of the overall credit risk management framework, the Firm focuses on the management and diversification of its industry and client exposures, with particular attention paid to industries with an actual or potential credit concern.

comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for Credit Losses Trends and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses for loans and lending commitments remained relatively unchanged in 2024, driven by provisions for specific commercial real estate loans and corporate loan growth, offset by charge-offs mainly in the office sector and an improved macroeconomic outlook.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley disclose specific drivers for their corporate loan portfolios in 2024, highlighting growth in the corporate book. Goldman Sachs identifies Technology, Media & Telecommunications as its largest corporate loan concentration (24%), while Morgan Stanley notes that corporate loan portfolio growth was a key driver alongside provisions for specific commercial real estate loans in determining the allowance for credit losses.

sentences.text: • The top five industry concentrations for corporate loans as of December 2024 were 24% for technology, media & telecommunications, 16% for diversified industrials, 14% for real estate, 9% for financial institutions and 9% for healthcare.

The allowance for credit losses for loans and lending commitments was relatively unchanged in 2024, reflecting provisions for certain specific commercial real estate loans and growth in the corporate loan portfolio, offset by charge-offs related to commercial real estate lending, mainly in the office sector, and improvements in the macroeconomic outlook.
